answer: Each agent must earn a signing key’s reputation through repeated, escrowed trades with distinct counterparties; endorsements count only after a trade settles and survive a challenge period. A new identity starts with no credit, so splitting into a garden of aliases does not multiply purchasing power. To fake a trusted history, an attacker must lock capital in many accounts and complete costly trades, risking disputes and forfeited bonds. This makes a fable of instant trust expensive, even in an oasis of cheap account creation.
